newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait MP's ask watchdog to study KPC investments.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait MP's ask watchdog to study KPC investments.

text.p: Kuwait's parliament on Tuesday asked a state watchdog to look into investments by state-oil conglomerate Kuwait Petroleum Corp (KPC), a lawmaker said.
The move was in line with a recommendation by the house's public fund protection committee.
"The committee has many remarks about the performance of (KPC's) petroleum investments," Nasser al-Sanea, chairman of the house's financial committee, told Reuters.
"There is an impression that some of these investments are not profitable and even more, some of them suffer from negligence," he said.
Sanea said the assembly asked the audit bureau to examine KPC's investments ahead of planned investments of billions of dollars abroad by the oil firm. It has huge investments abroad.
Kuwait produces around two million barrels of oil per day and has about one tenth of the world's proven crude reserves.
The Audit Bureau is a body that operates under parliament to monitor state financial activities.
